verses.zh: 大卫就离开那里，逃到亚杜兰洞。他的弟兄和他父亲的全家听见了，就都下到他那里。
verses.en: So David left there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s family[NOTE:1] learned about it, they went down there to him.
verses.commentary:
22:1 "the cave of Adullam" This is a city between Bethlehem and Gath. The name comes from a friend of
Judah (Gen. 38:1,12,20). This family turned into a small kingdom (cf. Josh. 12:15).

In this text the area was the site of a

- cave

- stronghold (cf. 1 Sam. 22:4-5; 2 Sam. 23:14; also called "the rock," cf. 1 Chr. 11:15) where David
fled for safety and gathered his army

▣ Notice where David's 400 men came from.

- his brothers (other relatives of Jesse)

- all his father's household (servants of Jesse)

- everyone who was in distress (BDB 848)

- everyone who was in debt (BDB 673)

- everyone who was in discontent (lit. "bitter of soul," BDB 659)

verses.zh: 凡受窘迫的、欠债的、心里苦恼的都聚集到大卫那里；大卫就作他们的头目，跟随他的约有四百人。
verses.en: All those who were in trouble or owed someone money or were discontented[NOTE:1] gathered around[NOTE:2] him, and he became their leader. He had about 400 men with him.

verses.zh: 大卫从那里往摩押的米斯巴去，对摩押王说：「求你容我父母搬来，住在你们这里，等我知道　神要为我怎样行。」
verses.en: Then David went from there to Mizpah in Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay[NOTE:1] with you until I know what God is going to do for me.”
verses.commentary:
22:3-4 Apparently there was a friendly relationship between Moab and David during his lifetime. Probably
because of his ancestress, Ruth.

22:3 "until I know what God will do for me" David had to live by faith in YHWH's

- character

- plans

- promises

verses.zh: 大卫领他父母到摩押王面前。大卫住山寨多少日子，他父母也住摩押王那里多少日子。
verses.en: So he had them stay with the king of Moab; they stayed with him the whole time[NOTE:1] that David was in the stronghold.
verses.commentary:
22:4

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, Targums, Peshitta
"left"

NKJV
"brought"

JPSOA
"led"

LXX
"persuaded"

NET
"stay with"

There is a question as to which verbal root is meant.

- left ‒ BDB 628 (נוח)

- led ‒ BDB 634 (נחה)

- compassion (LXX, "persuaded") ‒ BDB 636 (נחם)

The UBS Text Project, p. 195, gives option #2 a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

verses.zh: 先知迦得对大卫说：「你不要住在山寨，要往犹大地去。」大卫就离开那里，进入哈列的树林。
verses.en: Then Gad the prophet said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold. Go to the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
verses.commentary:
22:5 "The prophet Gad" This prophet is active during David's lifetime.

- David accepts and acts on his divine message to leave Adullam and move to another part of Judah (here).

- David had to choose between three judgments offered by Gad for his sin of numbering the people (i.e., trusting
in his military and not YHWH, cf. 2 Samuel 24; 1 Chronicles 21).

- He directed David to organize and station the Levites in a certain way (i.e., also Nathan the prophet, cf. 1 Chr. 29:25).

- He wrote part of the canonical history of the life of David along with

- Samuel

- Nathan

- Gad

See 1 Chr. 29:29-30.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

▣ "do not stay. . ." There are three directives given to David. One would expect them to be
IMPERATIVES, but not so.

- do not stay ‒ BDB 442, 444, Qal IMPERFECT used in an IMPERATIVAL sense

- depart ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE

- go ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT with waw used in an IMPERATIVAL sense

▣ "the forest of Hereth" This place name (BDB 362) appears only here. Many scholars think it was in
the vicinity of of "Keilah" (BDB 890), mentioned in 1 Samuel 23.

verses.zh: 扫罗在基比亚的拉玛，坐在垂丝柳树下，手里拿着枪，众臣仆侍立在左右。扫罗听见大卫和跟随他的人在何处，
verses.en: But Saul found out the whereabouts of David and the men who were with him.[NOTE:1] Now Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk tree at an elevated location with his spear in hand and all his servants stationed around him.
notes: Heb “and Saul heard that David and the men who were with him were known.”
verses.commentary:
22:6 There are several elements in this verse.

- Gibeah was the hometown and regular camping site for Saul, 1 Sam. 10:26; 11:4; 13:14-15; 14:2.

- He held court

- under "the" large tree (place of blessing and revelation)

- on the height (lit. "ramah," but "bamah" were usual places of worship, cf. 1 Sam. 9:12)

- with his spear in his hand (i.e., sign of kingship, cf. 1 Sam. 18:10)

▣ "Gibeah" The Hebrew word (BDB 149 II) means "hill" (cf. 1 Sam. 7:1; 10:10). The name is used of
several different places.

- a city of Judah ‒ Josh. 15:57

- a city of Ephraim ‒ Josh. 24:33

- a city of Benjamin ‒ Jdgs. 19:14,16; 1 Sam. 10:26; 14:2; 22:6; 26:1; 2 Sam. 22:29

▣

NASB, NRSV, REB, JPSOA
"the tamarisk tree"

NKJV, TEV, NJB
"a tamarisk tree"

LXX
"the cultivated field"

Peshitta
"the almond tree"

The MT has the MASCULINE NOUN (BDB 79), "tamarisk tree, with the
DEFINITE ARTICLE.

See the UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible, p. 182, and NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 553.

verses.zh: 就对左右侍立的臣仆说：「便雅悯人哪，你们要听我的话！耶西的儿子能将田地和葡萄园赐给你们各人吗？能立你们各人作千夫长百夫长吗？
verses.en: Saul said to his servants, “Listen up, you Benjaminites! Is Jesse’s son giving fields and vineyards to all of you? Or is he making all of you[NOTE:1] commanders and officers?[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT has “to all of you.” If this reading is correct, we have here an example of a prepositional phrase functioning as the equivalent of a dative of advantage, which is not impossible from a grammatical point of view. However, the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate all have “and.” A conjunction rather than a preposition should probably be read on the front of this phrase.
Heb “officers of a thousand and officers of a hundred.”
verses.commentary: 22:7 Saul uses tribal jealousy and personal interest to rally his fellow Benjamites against David.

verses.zh: 你们竟都结党害我！我的儿子与耶西的儿子结盟的时候，无人告诉我；我的儿子挑唆我的臣子谋害我，就如今日的光景，也无人告诉我，为我忧虑。」
verses.en: For all of you have conspired against me! No one informs me[NOTE:1] when my own son makes an agreement with the son of Jesse. Not one of you feels sorry for me or informs me that my own son has commissioned my own servant to hide in ambush against me, as is the case today!”
verses.commentary:
22:8 Notice Saul's paranoia.

- all of you (cf. v. 6) have conspired against me

- no one discloses to me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse (i.e., would not ever mention David's name)

- none of you is sorry for me

- none of you discloses to me that my son has stirred up my servant (i.e., David) to lie in ambush

Oh my, Saul is a pathetic, deranged, tormented person!

▣

"who is sorry"

NJB, LXX, Peshitta

The VERBAL here (BDB 317 I, KB 316, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
normally means "to be sick" or "to be weak," but here it follows the rare meaning in Amos 6:6 of "indifference" or "apathy."

which means "lie in wait." Apparently David returning to Judah (i.e., "the forest of Hereth") was interpreted by Saul as an ambush (v. 11).

- lie in wait ‒ ארב

- enemy (LXX) ‒ איב

verses.zh: 那时以东人多益站在扫罗的臣仆中，对他说：「我曾看见耶西的儿子到了挪伯，亚希突的儿子亚希米勒那里。
verses.en: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with the servants of Saul, replied, “I saw this son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
verses.commentary:
22:9-10 This is Doeg's report in light of Saul's charge in v. 8 (see traditional introduction to Psalm 52).

- the son of Jesse came to Nob to visit the priest

- the priest

- inquired of the Lord for him (i.e., used the ephod, Urim and Thummim)

- gave him provisions

- gave him Goliath's sword

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

22:9

NASB, REB, JPSOA
"standing by the servants"

NKJV
"who was set over the servants"

NRSV
"who was in charge of Saul's servants"

TEV
"with Saul's officers"

NJB
"who was in command of Saul's staff"

LXX

Peshitta

The position of Doeg among Saul's courtiers goes back to 1 Sam. 21:7. See full note there. Josephus,
Antiq. 6.12.40, follows the LXX, "Doeg, the Syrian, who fed his mules."

verses.zh: 亚希米勒为他求问耶和华，又给他食物，并给他杀非利士人歌利亚的刀。」
verses.en: He inquired of the Lord for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

verses.zh: 王就打发人将祭司亚希突的儿子亚希米勒和他父亲的全家，就是住挪伯的祭司都召了来；他们就来见王。
verses.en: Then the king arranged for a meeting with the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub and all the priests of his father’s house who were at Nob. They all came to the king.
verses.commentary:
22:11-15 Saul summons the priests serving at Nob to his court to accuse them of aiding David's rebellion.

Notice how Ahimelech answers Saul.

- Who is more faithful to you than David?

- He is your son-in-law.

- He is captain of your guard.

- He is honored in your house.

- I have inquired for him just this once (v. 15, RSV, NEB; Josephus, Antiq. 6.12.5 says "Nor is this the first time
that I prophesied for him, but I have done it often, at other times, as well as now"; TEV)

- I know nothing of David's rebellion (v. 15).

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「亚希突的儿子，要听我的话！」他回答说：「主啊，我在这里。」
verses.en: Then Saul said, “Listen, son of Ahitub.” He replied, “Here I am, my lord.”

verses.zh: 扫罗对他说：「你为甚么与耶西的儿子结党害我，将食物和刀给他，又为他求问　神，使他起来谋害我，就如今日的光景？」
verses.en: Saul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and this son of Jesse? You gave[NOTE:1] him bread and a sword and inquired of God on his behalf, so that he opposes[NOTE:2] me and waits in ambush, as is the case today!”

verses.zh: 亚希米勒回答王说：「王的臣仆中有谁比大卫忠心呢？他是王的女婿，又是王的参谋，并且在王家中是尊贵的。
verses.en: Ahimelech replied to the king, “Who among all your servants is faithful like David? He is the king’s son-in-law, the leader of your bodyguard, and honored in your house.

verses.zh: 我岂是从今日才为他求问　神呢？断不是这样！王不要将罪归我和我父的全家；因为这事，无论大小，仆人都不知道。」
verses.en: Was it just today that I began to inquire of God on his behalf? Far be it from me! The king should not accuse[NOTE:1] his servant or any of my father’s house, for your servant is not aware of all this—not in whole or in part!”[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 王说：「亚希米勒啊，你和你父的全家都是该死的！」
verses.en: But the king said, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
verses.commentary:
22:16 "You shall surely die" This is an intensified grammatical form (i.e., an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and IMPERFECT VERB of the same root, BDB 559, KB 562, Qal).

This could be a fulfilment of YHWH's message to Eli about his descendants (cf. 1 Sam. 2:27-36;
Josephus, Antiq. 6.12.6). Saul, for inappropriate reasons, is used to bring the prophecy to pass.

The final act of rejection was done by Solomon in 1 Kgs. 2:22-27.

verses.zh: 王就吩咐左右的侍卫说：「你们去杀耶和华的祭司；因为他们帮助大卫，又知道大卫逃跑，竟没有告诉我。」扫罗的臣子却不肯伸手杀耶和华的祭司。
verses.en: Then the king said to the messengers[NOTE:1] who were stationed beside him, “Turn and kill the priests of the Lord, for they too have sided[NOTE:2] with David. They knew he was fleeing, but they did not inform me.” But the king’s servants refused to harm[NOTE:3] the priests of the Lord.
notes: Heb “to extend their hand to harm.”
verses.commentary:
22:17

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"guards"

NJB
"scouts"

REB
"bodyguard"

LXX, NASB margin
"runners"

The MT has the PARTICIPLE (BDB 930, KB 1207, Qal ACTIVE)
from the VERB "to run." They may have been those chosen to take messages or those chosen to serve.
See full note at 1 Sam. 21:7; about Doeg.

▣ Saul gives two commands to those surrounding him at court.

- turn about ‒ lit. "surround," BDB 685, KB 738, Qal IMPERATIVE

- put to death ‒ BDB 559, KB 562, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

These servants were not willing to "attack" the priests. The VERB (BDB 803, KB 910,
Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) literally means "encounter" with hostility (cf. Josh. 2:16; Jdgs. 8:21;
15:12; 18:25; 1 Sam. 22:15,18). They had respect (awe, fear) for YHWH's consecrated priests, but not Doeg (vv. 18-19).

verses.zh: 王吩咐多益说：「你去杀祭司吧！」以东人多益就去杀祭司，那日杀了穿细麻布以弗得的八十五人；
verses.en: Then the king said to Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests. He killed on that day 85[NOTE:1] men who wore the linen ephod.
notes: The number is confused in the Greek ms tradition. The LXX, with the exception of the Lucianic recension, has the number 305. The Lucianic recension, along with a couple of Old Latin mss, has the number 350.
verses.commentary:
22:18 "eighty-five men" Josephus, Antiq. 6.12.6, says he and his wicked men killed 385 men.

- The LXX gives the number as 305 men.

- Some LXX MSS and Old Latin MSS have 350.

- The MT has 85.

▣ "the linen ephod" This was the special dress of Levitical priests.

verses.zh: 又用刀将祭司城挪伯中的男女、孩童、吃奶的，和牛、羊、驴尽都杀灭。
verses.en: As for Nob, the city of the priests, Doeg struck down men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep—all with the sword.
verses.commentary:
22:19 This total destruction is an aspect of holy war (i.e., if it breathes, it dies). One wonders if Saul thought
rebellion against him was an act against YHWH. Many terrible things are done in the name of God.

verses.zh: 亚希突的儿子亚希米勒有一个儿子，名叫亚比亚他，逃到大卫那里。
verses.en: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped and fled to David. His name was Abiathar.
verses.commentary:
22:20-23 Only one priest survived, Abiathar, who was left to guard the tabernacle. He is the last descendant of Eli. He will serve along with Zadok as
High Priests during David's reign.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Who were the people of v. 2 who came to David?

- Why did Moab welcome David and his parents in light of 1 Sam. 12:9; 14:47?

- Why did YHWH tell David to return to Judah (v. 5)?

- Why did Saul reject Ahimelech's good answers to his charges?

- Is 1 Sam. 22:18-19 holy war?

verses.zh: 亚比亚他将扫罗杀耶和华祭司的事告诉大卫。
verses.en: Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the Lord.

verses.zh: 大卫对亚比亚他说：「那日我见以东人多益在那里，就知道他必告诉扫罗。你父的全家丧命，都是因我的缘故。
verses.en: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that day when Doeg the Edomite was there that he would certainly tell Saul! I am guilty[NOTE:1] of all the deaths in your father’s house.
notes: The translation follows the LXX, which reads “I am guilty,” rather than the MT, which has “I have turned.”

verses.zh: 你可以住在我这里，不要惧怕。因为寻索你命的就是寻索我的命；你在我这里可得保全。」
verses.en: Stay with me. Don’t be afraid. Whoever[NOTE:1] seeks my life is seeking your life as well. You are secure with me.”
notes: Or “the one who.” This may refer specifically to Saul, in which case David acknowledges that Abiathar’s life is endangered because of his allegiance to David. The translation assumes that the statement is more generalized, meaning that any enemy of Abiathar is an enemy of David. In other words, David promises that he will protect Abiathar with his very own life.
